Once upon a time a little girl lived near a big green wood.
She always wore a bright red hood that her grandmother had made, so everyone called her Red Riding Hood.
One morning her mother packed a basket of cakes and honey.
Take this basket to your grandmother, who is not feeling well,
said Mother.
Go straight along the path, and do not talk to strangers.
I will be careful,
said Red Riding Hood, and off she went.
In the wood Red Riding Hood met a big grey Wolf.
He had a sly smile and shiny teeth.
Good morning, little girl,
said Wolf.
Where are you going so early?
I am taking cakes and honey to my grandmother,
said Red Riding Hood.
She lives in the cottage by the old oak tree.
What a lovely idea,
Why not pick some flowers for her too?
There are pretty ones in that meadow.
Red Riding Hood stopped to pick flowers.
Meanwhile the Wolf ran as fast as he could to the cottage by the old oak tree.
Knock, knock!
The Wolf knocked on the door.
Who is there?
said Grandmother.
It is Red Riding Hood,
said Wolf in a soft little voice.
Grandmother opened the door, and the Wolf jumped inside.
He shut her in the big wardrobe, put on her nightcap and climbed into her bed.
Soon Red Riding Hood came to the cottage with her flowers.
She went in and walked up to the bed.
Grandmother, what big ears you have!
All the better to hear you with,
Grandmother, what big eyes you have!
All the better to see you with,
Grandmother, what big teeth you have!
All the better to scare you with!
said Wolf, and he jumped out of the bed.
Help!
cried Red Riding Hood, and she ran out of the door.
A Woodcutter was chopping wood nearby.
He heard the shout and came running with his big axe.
Stop right there, Wolf!
said Woodcutter.
That is no way to treat a little girl.
The Wolf took one look at the axe, and he ran away into the wood as fast as his legs could carry him.
He never came back.
The Woodcutter opened the wardrobe, and out came Grandmother, quite safe.
Thank you, dear Woodcutter,
And thank you for coming, my little Red Riding Hood.
I will never talk to strangers again,
They all sat down together and ate the cakes and honey.
